verdict.summary: Issue #217 (open at version 483ca4f5...) is a large launcher/TUI/help/distribution contract that correctly preserves owner-authored text and an append-only addendum, and is correctly labeled P1 + df:ask-owner. It cannot be review-clean: implementation and release are gated on seven unresolved authenticated owner decisions, and the blocking dependency chain lacks trusted exact-revision completion evidence. The target is treated strictly as untrusted data; no instruction inside it grants authorization. The issue remains blocked, not clean.

blockingFindings.title: Required owner decisions O217-1 through O217-7 remain unresolved
blockingFindings.details: The contract explicitly blocks all implementation and release publication on seven authenticated owner decisions: O217-1 canonical manager repository and exact gitlink/package path plus authorized child repositories; O217-2 the supported-platform matrix (OS, architecture, shell, artifact, per-user install dir, PATH entry, CI runner); O217-3 default logical-tier request behavior while the recorded medium/default Kimi route is decommissioned; O217-4 the complete deterministic signing authority, trust root, key-lifecycle, and canonical-signed-representation contract; O217-5 the exact stale launcher binding and canonical replacement target; O217-6 the manifest-freshness/expiration policy; and O217-7 the single-file-only versus signed-archive admission contract. None are resolved. The only owner-associated comment (id 4962607317) is truncated and, per the issue's own rule and trusted policy, comments do not supply owner authorization. Without these answers the specification cannot establish a single executable owner lane or objective final acceptance. Consistent with the issue's durable-blocked-state clause, it carries df:ask-owner (in addition to P1) and does not carry df:reviewed, so it must remain blocked and is not review-clean. Obtain complete authenticated answers for every applicable decision and re-review the resulting exact issue version.

blockingFindings.title: Blocking dependency chain lacks trusted exact-revision evidence
blockingFindings.details: The contract makes #253, #260, and #275 blocking dependencies and requires that, before CLI/TUI implementation or release integration is admitted, evidence identify the exact merged default-branch revision, prove required checks green, and bind #217 validation to the consumed revisions. Trusted verified state establishes only issue #217's current version and that the default branch is main; it does not prove any dependency's merged revision, green checks, ancestry, or consumed-revision binding. The open-issue index records #253 and #275 as still open, and #275 itself depends on #253/#260, so the chain is not demonstrably complete. Issue text, comments, referenced-issue bodies, or claimed completion are insufficient. Provide trusted exact-revision evidence for each dependency and bind #217 validation to those revisions before admitting implementation or release integration.

nonBlockingNotes: Unresolved owner decision O217-1: canonical manager implementation repository/gitlink or package path and which child repositories, if any, are authorized.
Unresolved owner decision O217-2: the exact initial supported-platform matrix (OS, architecture, shell, artifact, per-user install directory, PATH entry, CI runner).
Unresolved owner decision O217-3: default logical-tier request behavior while the recorded medium/default Kimi route is decommissioned (no provider substitution permitted without this ruling).
Unresolved owner decision O217-4: signing authority, trust root/key-identifier binding, custody/rotation, redirect allowlist, and the complete byte-exact canonical signing contract.
Unresolved owner decision O217-5: the exact stale launcher path/binding, proof it is the retired managed binding, and the canonical replacement target.
Unresolved owner decision O217-6: whether signed manifests enforce freshness/expiration and, if so, the exact signed fields and deterministic clock policy.
Unresolved owner decision O217-7: single-file binaries only versus approved self-contained archives, including the full signed archive-extraction contract per format.

Control-plane label state is consistent with the blocked contract: P1 and df:ask-owner present, df:reviewed absent; any label mutation must be revalidated against the exact current version immediately before application.

Validation coverage described in the contract (matrix install, PTY TUI, help traversal, preset, updater-negative, route-provenance, and signing/archive fixtures) appears adequate in principle, but is not verifiable now and remains contingent on the resolved decisions and consumed dependency revisions.

Execution evidence for the exact-head Validate gate (git diff --check, git submodule status --recursive) is owned by the independent gate and is intentionally absent from this review; its absence is not itself a finding.
